subject: Rate/econ readout & next steps — BrightCart pricing and overage options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jared Kim <jared.kim@brightcart.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Rate/econ readout + next steps from today's call

Samantha — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the items I promised to follow up on.

Key signals from the call:
- Primary workload: checkout fraud scoring + conversational product help (mixed prompts). Estimated median request size ~350 tokens, peak session sizes up to ~2.5k tokens for long context.
- Steady-state expected: ~12M tokens/month across staging + prod in Q3.
- Burst pattern: marketing spikes (campaigns) create short 6–12 hour 2–3x increases a few times per month; anticipated single-day max ~6–8M tokens.
- Target budget range: $6k–$10k/month initially (Band indicates willingness to pay ~ $6–8k if unit economics align).
- Target unit goal: aim for $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens (net effective after committed discount), subject to model/quantization choice.

Rate/overage constraints you flagged:
1) Need a burst cushion to avoid immediate throttling during campaign spikes. Prefer a soft-burst (short-term allowance) rather than immediate hard cap.
2) Procurement needs deterministic overage math (simple $/1M overage tiers and monthly cap).
3) Legal will want language around sustained overage behavior and auto-scale protections.

Action items I committed to: 
- Share a concise pricing tab that shows: committed tier, effective $/1M tokens, burst window (hours), and overage tiers. (Attachment: BrightCart_Redwood_Pricing_v3.pdf)
- Propose a mutual action plan with milestones and a recommended pilot capacity for Q3. (Attachment: BrightCart_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx)
- Internal ask: loop in Ben for discount approval if BrightCart lands at the top of their budget band.

Proposed interim plan (quick):
- Pilot — 6M committed tokens/month for 90 days. Effective target price: $1,050 / 1M tokens (includes 15% committed discount + basic batch/cache recommendations).
- Burst handling — soft buffer: allow up to 2x committed for 12 hours (no charge beyond committed for the first 12 hours), then overage tier 1: $1,800 / 1M for next 5M tokens that month, tier 2: $2,800 / 1M beyond that. Monthly hard cap option available to stop overage after organization approval.

Please confirm: (1) the pilot committed size looks reasonable, (2) the burst window matches your operational needs, and (3) procurement/finance preferred way to model the overage cap (hard stop vs. negotiated cap + approval).

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0184

--
Attachment stubs: BrightCart_Redwood_Pricing_v3.pdf (11 pages, pricing table), BrightCart_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (MMP template)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Kim <jared.kim@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate/econ readout + next steps from today's call

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. That pilot outline aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token math: our 12M/mo estimate is conservative for Q3 — hitting 20M/mo by Q4 is plausible if the campaign succeeds. Can you show a simple 12/20/30M token tier comparison in the pricing PDF? We want to see how unit price moves with commit.

2) Burst behavior: the 12-hour soft buffer makes sense. Two questions: does the soft buffer apply per project (we have two projects) or per account? Also, can we cap daily burst cost so we don't get surprised before procurement signs off?

3) Overages: procurement prefers a single overage tier rather than multiple micro-tiers if the math is simple to audit. If the math is tiered, please provide a formula we can export to our cost model.

4) Regarding the $900–$1,200 / 1M target — that is a helpful target, but we need to see sample effective pricing lines for the specific models you recommended (small-quantized open model vs. larger full-precision variant).

I'll loop procurement on follow-ups — adding procurement@brightcart.com. Jared, can you confirm the legal/finance cadence for approving a hard monthly cap vs. soft overage?

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Growth, BrightCart
Samantha.ortiz@brightcart.com

Marcus / Samantha — procurement here. A few concrete asks so we can move this to legal review: 

- Please provide a short attachment (one page) that shows: committed tokens, effective $/1M, burst allowance (hours and multiplier), and the overage price formula. Our legal team wants a single page we can paste into the SOW.
- For accounting, we need the monthly invoicing cadence and a sample invoice line item (how you display committed vs. overage).
- For the hard cap option: what is the customer experience if the cap is reached (do API calls return 429, or do you queue them)? We need explicit behavior documented.

If possible, can you respond with the one-pager and a sample invoice line by EOD tomorrow? Ben — looping you for pricing confirmation.

Thanks — Procurement, BrightCart
procurement@brightcart.com

> On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 12:03 PM Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@brightcart.com> wrote:
> > Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. That pilot outline aligns with what we discussed.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate/econ readout + next steps from today's call

Procurement / Samantha — appreciate the clear asks. Attached I am sending: (1) a one-page pricing snapshot that mirrors the pilot proposal and two alternate commit tiers (12M / 20M / 30M), (2) a sample invoice line and (3) the mutual action plan. See attachments and bullet summary below.

Summary (answers to procurement):
- One-pager: committed tokens and effective unit price for three commit levels: 12M ($1,050 / 1M), 20M ($950 / 1M), 30M ($850 / 1M). These assume the quantized model and include a standard committed-discount schedule.
- Burst allowance: soft buffer applies at the account level; buffer is 2x committed for up to 12 hours. Soft buffer is not per-project by default but we can scope buffers to projects in Dedicated deployments.
- Overage math: simple step function we provide as a CSV formula. Example: if consumed > committed + soft_buffer_within_month then overage = (consumed - committed - soft_buffer_first_12h) * overage_rate. For the one-pager option we present a flat single overage tier at $1,800 / 1M for simplicity.
- Hard cap experience: by default we return 429 when the hard monthly cap is reached. We also offer an enterprise option to queue with a graceful degraded model (lower-capacity endpoints) — requires Dedicated config.
- Invoicing: monthly billing in arrears. Invoice line example: 
  "Committed capacity — 12,000,000 tokens @ $1,050 per 1M = $12,600"
  "Overage — 2,400,000 tokens @ $1,800 per 1M = $4,320"

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement confirms whether they prefer single overage tier (we recommend single $1,800 / 1M for pilot simplicity).
2) If yes, procurement confirms preferred hard cap amount (or opts for no hard cap but alerts).
3) We provide SOW language and a short Data Processing Appendix for review.

Ben — can you confirm the pricing lines above and sign off to lock pricing for the trial? If there is room to move the pilot price down to $975/1M for 12M commitment we can do that with a 6-month commit add-on.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
